items.q: She ____ to work by bus every day.
items.w: Third person singular in the present simple takes -s: he/she/it goes.

items.q: Be quiet — the baby ____.
items.w: Something happening right now takes the present continuous: is + -ing.

items.q: We ____ the match last Friday.
items.w: A finished time ("last Friday") takes the past simple.

items.q: I ____ in this city since 2019.
items.w: "Since" marks something starting in the past and still true: present perfect.

items.q: ____ you ever ____ to Japan?
items.w: Life experience with no stated time takes the present perfect: have been.

items.q: I ____ dinner when the phone rang.
items.w: A longer action interrupted by a shorter one takes the past continuous.

items.q: By the time we arrived, the film ____.
items.w: The earlier of two past events takes the past perfect: had started.

items.q: Look at those clouds — it ____ rain.
items.w: Present evidence for a future event takes "going to", not "will".

items.q: By next June I ____ here for ten years.
items.w: Completed before a future point: will have + past participle.

items.q: My eyes hurt — I ____ at this screen all morning.
items.w: An action continuing up to now, with the duration in focus, takes have been + -ing.

items.q: She is ____ engineer at a shipping firm.
items.w: "An" before a vowel sound: an engineer.

items.q: ____ sun rose at six.
items.w: Unique things take "the": the sun, the moon, the earth.

items.q: I do not drink ____ coffee in the evening.
items.w: An uncountable noun in a general sense takes no article.

items.q: There is not ____ milk left.
items.w: "Much" goes with uncountable nouns; "many" with countable ones.

items.q: ____ of my friends live abroad.
items.w: "Several" takes a plural countable noun and a plural verb.

items.q: She has ____ patience for excuses.
items.w: "Little" (without "a") means almost none, and pairs with an uncountable noun.

items.q: The meeting is ____ Monday morning.
items.w: Days and dates take "on": on Monday.

items.q: We will be there ____ six o'clock.
items.w: Clock times take "at": at six o'clock.

items.q: She has worked here ____ three years.
items.w: "For" takes a length of time; "since" takes a starting point.

items.q: He is very good ____ explaining difficult ideas.
items.w: "Good at" is the fixed pairing, and a verb after a preposition takes -ing.

items.q: The decision depends ____ the budget.
items.w: "Depend" is always followed by "on".

items.q: I must apologise ____ being late.
items.w: You apologise TO a person FOR a thing.

items.q: If it ____ tomorrow, we will stay in.
items.w: First conditional: if + present simple, then will + infinitive. Never "will" in the if-clause.

items.q: If I ____ you, I would take the job.
items.w: The second conditional uses "were" for every person: if I were you.

items.q: If she ____ harder, she would have passed.
items.w: Third conditional: if + past perfect, then would have + past participle.

items.q: If I had taken that job, I ____ in Dhaka now.
items.w: A past condition with a present result: had + past participle, then would + infinitive.

items.q: You ____ smoke in the hospital.
items.w: Modals take no auxiliary and no "to": must not smoke.

items.q: You ____ be tired after that journey.
items.w: "Must" expresses a confident deduction, not only obligation.

items.q: I ____ swim when I was six.
items.w: "Could" is the past of general ability.

items.q: She ____ the email — she never received it.
items.w: "Cannot have + past participle" expresses certainty that something did NOT happen.

items.q: You ____ told me — I would have helped.
items.w: "Should have + past participle" is regret about the past.

items.q: The bridge ____ in 1890.
items.w: Passive past simple: was/were + past participle.

items.q: The results ____ tomorrow.
items.w: The results receive the action, so the passive is needed: will be announced.

items.q: She said she ____ tired.
items.w: Reported speech shifts the tense back one step: "I am" becomes "she was".

items.q: He asked me where ____.
items.w: A reported question takes statement word order and a backshifted tense.

items.q: The man ____ car was stolen called the police.
items.w: "Whose" marks possession: the man whose car.

items.q: The book, ____ I read last year, is still my favourite.
items.w: A non-defining clause after a comma takes "which", never "that".

items.q: I really enjoy ____ early.
items.w: "Enjoy" is always followed by the -ing form.

items.q: She agreed ____ the report by Friday.
items.w: "Agree" is followed by the infinitive with "to".

items.q: I stopped ____ coffee because it kept me awake.
items.w: "Stop + -ing" means you ended the habit; "stop to drink" means you paused in order to drink.

items.q: Not only ____ late, but he also forgot the tickets.
items.w: A negative adverbial at the front inverts the subject and auxiliary: was he.

items.q: This exam was ____ than the last one.
items.w: Adjectives of three or more syllables take "more", not "-er".

items.q: It is ____ film I have ever seen.
items.w: A superlative takes "the": the best.

items.q: Each of the students ____ a folder.
items.w: "Each" is singular however many follow it, so the verb is singular.

items.q: The news ____ better today.
items.w: "News" looks plural but takes a singular verb.

items.q: Neither the manager nor the staff ____ been told.
items.w: With "neither…nor", the verb agrees with the nearer subject: staff have.

items.q: She ____ goes to bed before midnight.
items.w: Adverbs of frequency go before the main verb: she never goes.

items.q: I have ____ finished the first chapter.
items.w: "Already" is used in affirmative sentences; "yet" belongs in questions and negatives.

items.q: The rain did not ____ our plans.
items.w: "Affect" is the verb; "effect" is normally the noun.

items.q: There are ____ chairs than people.
items.w: "Fewer" for countable nouns, "less" for uncountable ones.

items.q: ____ going to be a long meeting.
items.w: "It's" is "it is". "Its" without an apostrophe is the possessive.

items.q: The company laid ____ two hundred workers.
items.w: "Lay off" means to make redundant.

items.q: I am looking forward to ____ from you.
items.w: "Looking forward to" ends in a preposition, so the verb takes -ing.

items.q: The evidence ____ the theory.
items.w: "Corroborate" means to support with evidence; "collaborate" means to work together.
